ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a three-state signal flow graph. On the left side there are two external input branches, respectively entering the corresponding summing/state input nodes with unit gain. In the figure there are three state-related nodes/integrator outputs, and the branch labels include upper feedback -α, lower feedback -γ, oblique couplings -β and β, as well as α and γ labels related to the right-side integrator/output. Below are given four options A, B, C, D, where the state matrix and input matrix of option D are respectively A = [[-γ, 0, β], [0, α, 0], [-β, 0, -α]], B = [[0, 1], [0, 0], [1, 0]]. Reasoning: According to the method specified in the problem, define the outputs of the three integrator/state nodes in order as x1, x2, x3. For each state derivative, only look at the arrows entering the input terminal of the corresponding integrator: the terms entering the input terminal corresponding to x1 are the self-feedback -γ x1, the coupling term β x3 from x3 through β, and the unit input u2, so x1_dot = -γ x1 + β x3 + u2. The only term entering the input terminal corresponding to x2 is α x2, so x2_dot = α x2. The terms entering the input terminal corresponding to x3 are the coupling term -β x1 from x1 through -β, the self-feedback -α x3, and the unit input u1, so x3_dot = -β x1 - α x3 + u1. From this, A = [[-γ, 0, β], [0, α, 0], [-β, 0, -α]], B = [[0, 1], [0, 0], [1, 0]] are formed, consistent with option D in the figure.

method.method_draft: Assign the state variables according to the outputs of the three integrator/state nodes shown in the graph. For each state derivative, inspect only the arrows that enter the corresponding integrator input node: include the self-feedback branch with its label, include cross-coupling branches with their signs, and include the external input branch if a unit arrow from u1 or u2 enters that summing point. This gives equations of the form dot x1 = -gamma x1 + beta x3 + u2, dot x2 = alpha x2, and dot x3 = -beta x1 - alpha x3 + u1 under the node ordering used in the options. Form the A and B matrices from these coefficients and compare them with options A-D; the matrix pair matches option D.
